No repo was checked out here, so I reproduced the exact structure in `/tmp/apgap004` (conftest + two live test files with the two fixture styles + normal tests) and ran it against a **local counting HTTP server** standing in for OpenRouter (logs one line per request). All runs used pytest 9.0.2 with a real-looking `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` exported.

| Scenario | Result | Network calls | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Default `pytest tests/` + key present | **3 passed, 6 skipped** (`-rs` shows `opt-in gate: pass --live-api or set PTP_LIVE=1` × 6) | **0** | 0.2s (no 30s hang) |
| `pytest tests/ --live-api` | 9 passed | 6 (all live tests ran) | 0.02s |
| `PTP_LIVE=1 pytest tests/` | 9 passed | +6 = 12 (all live tests ran) | 0.02s |
| Control A: `@pytest.mark.live` with **no** fixture gate | 1 passed — **API still called** | +1 = 13 | — |
| Control B: `--live-api` without `pytest_addoption` | `pytest: error: unrecognized arguments: --live-api` | 0 | — |
| Control B2: `getoption("--live-api")` without registration | `ValueError: no option named '--live-api'` | 0 | — |

Edge cases covered: both opt-in channels (flag and env) independently run all 6 live tests; default run makes zero socket connections even with the key present and completes in 0.2s; skip reason verified via `-rs` to prove the gate (not a key-missing skip) fired; mark-only gating proven insufficient (Control A); unregistered flag errors proven (Controls B/B2). This matches the reported repo outcome (3860 passed / 14 skipped, zero network) and generalizes the `_check_prereqs` autouse fixture pattern to the second file.
